claims.claim: Evals are defined in pack files and execute automatically during conversations or against recorded sessions.
Evals use the same check types as assertions and guardrails.
Evals can fire on every turn, on a sampled subset, or at session close.
Assertions only run during Arena tests.
Guardrails run inline before the response is delivered.
Eval handlers produce scores only, in the range 0.0 to 1.0.
Eval handlers never determine pass/fail; pass/fail belongs to assertion and guardrail wrappers.
When used as standalone evals, the score is recorded as a metric and emitted as an event.
Diagram edge: the Pack File (evals) feeds the EvalRunner.
Diagram edge: EvalRunner feeds the ResultWriter.
Diagram edge: ResultWriter writes to Metrics / Metadata.
Pack evals and scenario assertions share the same underlying check types.
Pack evals are defined in the pack file under an evals array.
Scenario assertions are defined in Arena scenario YAML.
Pack evals run in production and in testing.
Scenario assertions run in testing only.
Pack eval trigger is configurable with every turn, sampling, and session close options.
Scenario assertions run every turn or at conversation end.
Pack evals travel with the pack and run in production, in Arena tests, and anywhere the pack is used.
Scenario assertions are Arena-specific test expectations that validate conversation flows defined in test scenarios.
Each eval is an EvalDef object in the pack's evals array.
EvalDef field id is required and must be unique within the pack.
EvalDef field type is required and holds a check type from the checks reference.
EvalDef field trigger is required.
EvalDef field params is parameters specific to the check type.
EvalDef field threshold is optional and holds a pass/fail threshold such as min_score.
EvalDef field enabled is optional and defaults to true.
EvalDef field sample_percentage is optional and gives the percentage of turns or sessions to evaluate.
EvalDef field groups is optional and used for eval group filtering.
EvalDef field metric is optional and holds Prometheus metric configuration.
The example JSON eval definition uses id quality_check, type contains, trigger every_turn, params patterns thank you, threshold min_score 0.8, enabled true, sample_percentage 10, and a metric block.
The metric object in an eval definition has name, type, and labels fields.
Trigger value every_turn fires after each assistant response.
Trigger value on_session_complete fires when a session closes.
Trigger value sample_turns samples a percentage of turns using a hash.
Trigger value sample_sessions samples a percentage of sessions using a hash.
Trigger value on_conversation_complete fires when a multi-session conversation closes.
Trigger value on_workflow_step fires after a workflow state transition.
Sampling is deterministic: the same session ID and turn index always produce the same sampling decision.
Sampling uses an FNV-1a hash.
The toxicity_check example uses trigger sample_turns with sample_percentage 10 and params patterns harmful and offensive.
When no explicit groups are set, evals are automatically classified by handler type.
Group value default is assigned to all evals with no explicit groups.
Group value fast-running is assigned to contains, regex, json_valid, tools_called, and workflow checks.
Group value long-running is assigned to llm_judge, cosine_similarity, outcome_equivalent, a2a_eval, rest_eval, and exec handlers.
Group value external is assigned to llm_judge, a2a_eval, rest_eval, and exec handlers.
A contains eval with no explicit groups receives the groups default and fast-running.
An llm_judge eval with no explicit groups receives the groups default, long-running, and external.
Setting groups on an eval definition overrides the automatic classification entirely.
The compliance_check example uses type llm_judge, trigger every_turn, and groups compliance and safety.
An eval with explicit groups matches only filters for those groups and does not match default, long-running, or external.
The SDK uses EvalGroups to select which eval groups to run.
sdk.Evaluate takes a context and an sdk.EvaluateOpts value and returns results and an error.
sdk.EvaluateOpts has fields PackPath, Messages, and EvalGroups.
When EvalGroups is nil or empty, all evals run regardless of group.
The eval system supports three dispatch patterns: InProcDispatcher, EventDispatcher, and EventBusEvalListener.
InProcDispatcher runs evals synchronously in the same process.
InProcDispatcher is used by Arena and simple SDK deployments.
Diagram edges for InProcDispatcher: Conversation to InProcDispatcher, InProcDispatcher to EvalRunner, EvalRunner to Handlers, Handlers to ResultWriter.
EventDispatcher publishes eval requests to an event bus for async processing by workers.
EventDispatcher is used in production SDK deployments.
Diagram edges for EventDispatcher: Conversation to EventDispatcher, EventDispatcher to Event Bus, Event Bus to EvalWorker, EvalWorker to EvalRunner, EvalRunner to ResultWriter.
EventBusEvalListener subscribes to message.created EventBus events.
EventBusEvalListener triggers evals automatically without explicit middleware.

Diagram edges for EventBusEvalListener: RecordingStage to EventBus, EventBus to EventBusEvalListener, EventBusEvalListener to SessionAccumulator, SessionAccumulator to Dispatcher, Dispatcher to Runner.
SessionAccumulator accumulates messages per session and builds EvalContext on demand.
Sessions in the SessionAccumulator expire after a configurable TTL whose default is 30 minutes.
EvalConversationExecutor evaluates saved conversations from recordings.
EvalConversationExecutor step 1 loads the recording via the adapter registry.
EvalConversationExecutor step 2 builds conversation context from recorded messages.
EvalConversationExecutor step 3 applies turn-level assertions to each assistant message.
EvalConversationExecutor step 4 evaluates conversation-level assertions.
EvalConversationExecutor runs pack evals for every trigger if configured: turn evals per assistant turn, then session and conversation evals.
EvalConversationExecutor step 6 returns aggregated results.
The EvalConversationExecutor enables offline evaluation of historical conversations without re-running them against a live LLM.
Eval results are recorded as Prometheus metrics through the unified metrics.Collector into a prometheus.Registry, alongside pipeline metrics.
Import path github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus is used for the Prometheus registry.
Import path github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/runtime/v2/metrics exists at the version pinned in go.mod.
Import path github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/sdk/v2 exists at the version pinned in go.mod.
metrics.NewCollector takes a metrics.CollectorOpts value and returns a collector.
metrics.CollectorOpts has a Registerer field.
metrics.CollectorOpts has a Namespace field.
metrics.CollectorOpts has a ConstLabels field of type prometheus.Labels.
sdk.Open takes a pack path, a prompt name, and options, and returns a conversation.
sdk.WithMetrics takes a collector and a second argument, and is passed as an option to sdk.Open.
When WithMetrics is configured, all eval results are automatically recorded as Prometheus metrics alongside pipeline metrics.
Evals with an explicit metric definition use that configuration; evals without one get an auto-generated gauge metric named after the eval ID.
Eval metrics are namespaced under {namespace}_eval_.
A metric named response_quality_score with namespace myapp becomes myapp_eval_response_quality_score.
An eval with ID check-tone and no explicit metric becomes myapp_eval_check-tone.
Metric type gauge is set to the eval score value.
Metric type counter increments the count on each execution.
Metric type histogram observes the value with configurable buckets and tracks sum and count.
Metric type boolean records 1.0 if score is at least 1.0 and 0.0 otherwise.
Metric types are gauge, counter, histogram, and boolean.
Pack-author labels are declared in the metric.labels field of each eval definition.
The response_quality example metric uses name response_quality_score, type histogram, range min 0 and max 1.
The response_quality example metric labels are eval_type and category.
Const labels are set via CollectorOpts.ConstLabels and are process-level dimensions such as env and region.
Instance labels are set via CollectorOpts.InstanceLabels and bound per conversation, such as tenant and prompt_name.
Label names must match the regular expression ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$.
Label names must not start with a double underscore.
Invalid label names are caught during pack validation.
Event eval.completed uses the constant EventEvalCompleted.
Event eval.failed uses the constant EventEvalFailed.
eval.completed is emitted when an eval finishes successfully, regardless of score.
eval.failed is emitted when an eval handler returns an error.
EvalCompletedData payload carries the eval ID, type, score, and a derived Passed field.
IsPassed returns true when score is nil or at least 1.0.
A working eval that returns score 0.0 emits eval.completed, not eval.failed.
When both pack-level and prompt-level evals are defined, they are merged.
Prompt evals override pack evals where IDs match.
Pack-only evals are preserved in the merged set.
Prompt-only evals are appended to the merged set.
An eval-test example exists at examples/eval-test in the promptarena repository.
The eval-test example evaluates saved conversations with both deterministic assertions and llm_judge evals.
Internal link /arena/reference/assertions/ resolves to a page in this docs site.
Internal link /arena/explanation/session-recording/ resolves to a page in this docs site.

Arena scores every pack eval trigger at conversation end, replaying turn triggers once per assistant turn over the transcript up to that turn's reply; a turn ends at the assistant reply before the next user message.
